Effective eLoC: AI Tests are Longer and More Consistent.
Our analysis reveals that AI-generated tests have a slightly higher                      Semantic Analysis with Embeddings. To capture characteristics
median eLoC (12.0) compared to human-written tests (11.0). While                         beyond simple metrics, we visualized the semantic representations
the Mann-Whitney U test shows a statistically significant difference                     of the test methods using CodeBERT and t-SNE (Figure 2). By ana-
(𝑝 < 0.001), the calculated effect size is negligible (Cliff’s 𝛿 = −0.12),               lyzing the distribution of AI-authored tests in the semantic space,
suggesting the central tendencies are practically similar. However,                      we identified three distinct patterns of generation based on the spa-
a key observation lies in the variance and distribution (Figure 1a).                     tial relationship between AI-generated and human-authored tests:
Human-written tests exhibit a long tail of outliers with high eLoC                       (i) Dispersed Distribution, where AI tests are broadly scattered
(Max: 699), whereas AI tests are confined to a narrower range (Max:                      throughout the entire human test distribution, indicating struc-
87). This suggests that while typical length is comparable, AI agents                    tural similarity to various human styles (e.g., appkit, cal.com, and
generate code with higher consistency, avoiding the “massive” test                       capgo); (ii) Localized Distribution, where AI tests overlap with
methods that occasionally occur in human-authored code.                                  only specific clusters or regions of human tests (e.g., alchemy, liam,
                                                                                         primer-react, helper); and (iii) Isolated Distribution, where AI
